title: Rock, guitars and the star system
summary: Early rock sparked 'I can do that' attitudes and a star system.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: there was a point in the early sixties when very early rock, in its very primitive form, kind of spawned an attitude among a lot of young people, of gee, I can play this music too. You'd go out and have mommy and daddy buy you a guitar and you take ten lessons and after those ten lessons you're playing that music pretty much as it sounds on the record because it's extremely simple stuff.
That's when the guitar sales started to zoom upwards.
Then because of the stars involved, they had a star system immediately. That sort of thing was around a lot of time.
I remember in the forties, and the thirties, this sort of thing going on, but it wasn't so all encompassing as it is now.
